title: Integration technologies (middleware)
intro: Middleware is software that sits between applications and moves data and calls between them, so the applications do not need to know each other.

types.name: Message-oriented middleware (MOM)
types.purpose: Carries messages between applications through queues or topics, so sender and receiver do not need to be online at the same time.
types.example: RabbitMQ, Apache Kafka, Azure Service Bus
types.usedInPlanner: The queue that carries request.decided to the notifier (task T07).

types.name: Enterprise service bus (ESB)
types.purpose: A central bus that routes messages, translates formats and applies rules between many services.
types.usedInPlanner: Not used: too heavy for three services, but the idea of one shared channel is the same.

types.name: API gateway
types.purpose: One entry point for clients that forwards each call to the right service and adds security, limits and logging.
types.usedInPlanner: The gateway on port 4000 in front of the three services (episode 11).

types.name: ETL (extract, transform, load)
types.purpose: Copies data in batches from one system, reshapes it, and loads it into another, often a report or data warehouse.
types.example: Apache NiFi, Talend, a nightly script
types.usedInPlanner: Not used: the planner reads live data; ETL would fit a nightly report for Finance.

types.name: EAI hub
types.purpose: Enterprise application integration: one hub connects the applications, each through one adapter, instead of every pair talking directly.
types.usedInPlanner: The planner itself acts as a small hub for Student Affairs, Finance and Facilities.
